warnings.precise_source_claim: The index-weighted average is built from C_t.
warnings.warning: Both EMA lines print a bare C_t. It is not the close w_t and it has no gloss. The skill may write an exponential average of the closing price. It must not copy C_t or treat it as defined.

warnings.precise_source_claim: TRMA is a function of n_1 and averages TRIX over n_2 days.
warnings.warning: The left side carries n_1 while the sum is divided by n_2 and runs to n_2-1. The skill may average a smoothed series over its own window. It must not copy the mismatched argument.

warnings.precise_source_claim: The band width is the root of a sum of (w_i MA_i) times the departure.
warnings.warning: The factor (w_i MA_i) is printed with no operator, the sum runs from i=0 to n while dividing by n, and the middle band equals the previous day's average. The skill may write a band around a moving average. It must not copy the missing operator or the limits.

warnings.precise_source_claim: The cash update adds the proceeds of a sale and subtracts the cost of a purchase.
warnings.warning: Equation (8) puts the buy flag on the (1-alpha) term and the sell flag on the subtracted term. Equation (10), which claims to unpack it, does the reverse, and equation (25) follows equation (10). The skill may write cash that rises on a sale and falls on a purchase. It must not copy either line as the other's expansion.

warnings.precise_source_claim: The flags fire off the modified RSI.
warnings.warning: Equations (8) and (15) print the trigger as RST with a prime, while equation (13) prints RSI with a prime and the prose says the modified RSI. The skill may name the indicator once. It must not copy the RST spelling or treat the two marks as different indicators.

warnings.precise_source_claim: The MACD model only has to change the buy-sell test in equation (7).
warnings.warning: Equation (7) is the Bollinger formula, not the RSI test the program actually uses. Equations (16) and (17) also print DIF and DEA with no time argument and join the conditions with a bare italic and. The skill may swap one trigger test for another. It must not cite equation (7) as the test being replaced.

warnings.precise_source_claim: The portfolio variance uses the covariance at the same day as the weights.
warnings.warning: The covariance term indexes both weights and the covariance with k, while every other term uses t. The objective is also the square root of its own square, so the minimization has nothing to act on. The skill may minimize a portfolio variance. It must not copy the index or the identity.

warnings.precise_source_claim: The gates use a hyperbolic tangent.
warnings.warning: Equations (21) and (23) print the activation as the two words tan y, with a space, and equation (22) multiplies the carried cell state by F with no subscript. The skill may write a gated recurrence. It must not copy the spaced activation or the bare F.

warnings.precise_source_claim: A sale is forced when gold has fallen by a fifth.
warnings.warning: Both gold terms are printed x_i with a gd superscript, so the difference is zero and the test can never fire. The bitcoin numerator subtracts x_i rather than the previous day's price the gloss describes, and the gloss adds a stray roman x and a stray roman y. The skill may write a stop at a stated decline. It must not copy equation (24).

warnings.precise_source_claim: The gold flags obey the same bounds as the bitcoin flags.
warnings.warning: The last clause of inner line (6) bounds the sum of the two gold flags by the gold price, mixing a count of flags with a price. The skill may bound a buy flag and a sell flag by one. It must not copy that clause.

warnings.precise_source_claim: The tuned RSI earns $36,867 more than the untuned one.
warnings.warning: Figure 4's callouts read 92,783, 67,691 and 40,824, and no pair of them differs by 36,867. The skill may quote the prose margin with its page. It must not derive it from the callouts or present them as agreeing.

warnings.precise_source_claim: The best gold period is n=1.
warnings.warning: The prose reads n=1 off Figure 7, whose legend prints n=16, and the inset dates run from December back to July. The skill may cite one of the two periods. It must not reconcile them.

warnings.precise_source_claim: Gold votes with BOLL and bitcoin votes with WR.
warnings.warning: The prose gives gold DMA, RSI, MACD, TRIX and BOLL, and bitcoin DMA, RSI, MACD, TRIX and WR. Figure 9 prints the last factor of each list on the other box. The skill may quote the prose sets. It must not copy the figure's lists or merge the two.

Figure 14's axis is ticked from 0 to 14 while the bar labels are percentages up to 1374, so the bar length does not represent the label. The skill may quote a labeled return. It must not read a value off the axis.

warnings.precise_source_claim: The trade count falls as the transaction cost rises.
warnings.warning: Figure 15's right panel draws a gold trade count below zero, and neither panel is labeled, so the reader cannot tell which factor is which. The skill may describe the two behaviors the prose names. It must not read a count off that panel.

warnings.precise_source_claim: The KDJ gold strategy earned 0.48 percent a year.
warnings.warning: Table 2 pairs a terminal value of 1021 with an annualized yield of 0.48 percent, which five years of growth from 1000 does not give. The skill may report the printed terminal value. It must not recompute the yield or cite one as the source of the other.

warnings.precise_source_claim: The improved strategy finished 51.64 percent ahead.
warnings.warning: Page 18 prints $190,635.58, Table 4 prints 189,635.58, and neither ratio against 124,716.87 gives 51.64 percent. The skill may quote one total with its page. It must not reconcile the two or recompute the percentage.
The summary says six factors, while both voting sets in section 4.5.2 hold five and the seventh, KDJ, appears only in Table 2. The skill may say five factors vote. It must not repeat the six.
